newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Coalition six-pack to make politics more beerable.
newsitem.headline: Coalition six-pack to make politics more beerable.

text.p: Wellington's Backbencher Bar and Cafe has produced a limited edition "coalition six-pack" to celebrate the country's first MMP election.
Manager Hamish Nixon said labels with party logos and quips had been produced to go on existing brews. Only 200 bottles of each had been produced.

"People will be able to express their democratic rights through drinking the brew of their choice or join in the MMP spirit by sampling one of each of the parties through a coalition six-pack," Nixon said.

Picking the brew for each party wasn't difficult, he said. Many people believed Labour and National were both trying to create a modern image for themselves, but had become pale imitations of their former selves. Hence the choice of the clear alcoholic soda Vault mixed in either raspberry juice (Labour) or blue curacao (National).
Winston Peters' "very cool" image was matched with Ice Beer, and the Alliance, the party that played up its "green" credentials, with Steinlager Green.
For Act -- the party that had been a long time coming -- it was Long Brew.
Some ginger beer was found at the back of the cooler for the Christian Coalition.
